free_tier.stated: 10 GB free; VIP 3 TB and SVIP 6 TB. A new account that saves one shared file gets 1 TB: '新用户保存一次别人分享的文件，可获取1TB的空间容量'

per_object_cap.stated: Not published for the free tier. Downloads above 50 MB need a desktop-client user agent and a cookie, else the API answers 23018 download file size limit

retention.stated: Accounts frozen after 12 months without a login, with the storage reclaimed if not unfrozen within a month: '超过1年未登录 … 回收存储容量 … 文件丢失、数据清空'

egress.terms: No per-GB fee, but the free tier is shaped to 2 to 4 MB/s against about 50 MB/s on SVIP, and a third-party fetch service measured a free account at about 60 KB/s. Downloads above 50 MB need a client user agent and a cookie

tooling: no official open API. The reverse-engineered web API at drive-pc.quark.cn is what the OpenList quark driver uses; the netdisk-fast-download qk parser states that a logged-in cookie is mandatory; the OpenList docs warn quick-transfer now needs a local agent because of the speed limit
chaining: 10 GB times N phone-verified accounts, and the 1 TB saved-from-a-share bonus is per account and time-limited rather than a durable multiply.

limits.value: 2 to 4 MB/s on the free tier
12 months without a login freezes the account and reclaims the capacity
share downloads above 50 MB need a desktop-client user agent and a cookie

identity_cost.detail: mainland +86 only, and SVIP payment needs a Chinese identity document

reliability_note: The anonymous path gets metadata and not bytes: a share token and a full file listing with fid and share_fid_token come back with no cookie at all, and the download call is 404 on all four documented hosts. Download tickets are IP-bound, so a link minted on one host dies when replayed from another, which is why every public Quark parser rots within weeks

binding_note: 10 GB is 2% of the filter and 2 to 4 MB/s is 170 to 340 GB a day at best, so the quota and the shaping both fail. The shaping is the one that would still bind on a paid tier, and the identity gate sits in front of both.
notes: Quark has largely replaced Baidu Pan as the default share host on Chinese forums, which is why it is recorded in full. The finding that matters for a bridge builder is that the anonymous token lists a whole share and cannot move a byte, and that download tickets are IP-bound so a harvested cookie does not survive a replay.
